subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw expose a global `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` setting that changes bootstrap context for every main, subagent, and cron run, rather than keeping the current fixed session-type policy?
rationale: This is a new public configuration contract that controls standing agent instructions and context budget across session types; correctness alone cannot decide its desired scope, defaults, and long-term support burden.

options.title: Accept the feature after semantic alignment
options.body: Adopt the global setting after the resolver/default contract is made internally consistent and its user-facing configuration is documented.

options.title: Narrow the policy surface
options.body: Request a more targeted design, such as an owner-approved per-agent or explicit session-policy mechanism, before adding a global default.

options.title: Keep fixed defaults
options.body: Decline the new setting and retain the existing session-type bootstrap allowlists as the supported core behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept the feature after semantic alignment
recommendation.body: Adopt the global setting after the resolver/default contract is made internally consistent and its user-facing configuration is documented.
